  1. Gated and private models

Gated and private models

Llama, Gemma, Mistral, and private organization repositories all require a Hugging Face token.

Preparing access

  1. Sign in to Hugging Face and open the model page, for example meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
  2. Accept the license and wait for approval; some models approve instantly, others take hours.
  3. Create a read token at https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens.
  4. Verify access before deploying:
export HF_TOKEN="hf_replace_me"

curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN" \
  https://huggingface.co/api/models/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct

200 means access is granted. 401 means the token is wrong, 403 means the license is not accepted for that account.

Externally managed Secret

The recommended pattern: the chart references the Secret but never stores the token.

kubectl create namespace models
kubectl create secret generic hf-secret \
  --namespace models \
  --from-literal=HF_TOKEN="$HF_TOKEN"

namespace: models

hfSecret:
  enabled: true
  managed: false
  name: hf-secret

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: 32Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

Chart-managed Secret

Simpler for development. Never commit the token.

hfSecret:
  enabled: true
  managed: true
  name: hf-secret
  token: ""

helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \
  --namespace kserve --create-namespace \
  -f values.yaml \
  --set-string hfSecret.token="$HF_TOKEN"

A token passed this way is stored in the Helm release Secret. Anyone able to read Secrets in the release namespace can recover it.

Gated model examples 

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

  - name: gemma-9b
    model:
      uri: hf://google/gemma-2-9b-it
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

  - name: mistral-7b
    model:
      uri: hf://mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

CPU variants through the models list:

models:
  - name: vllm-gemma-3-4b
    runtime: kserve-vllm-cpu
    modelFormat: huggingface
    storageUri: hf://google/gemma-3-4b-it
    args:
      - --served-model-name
      - gemma-3-4b-it

Private organization repositories

Identical mechanism; the token must belong to a member with read access.

models:
  - name: internal-classifier
    runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver
    modelFormat: huggingface
    storageUri: hf://my-org/internal-classifier
    args:
      - --task=sequence_classification

Different tokens per workload

Disable automatic injection and set the variable explicitly:

hfSecret:
  enabled: true
  managed: false
  name: hf-secret

models:
  - name: shared-model
    storageUri: hf://my-org/shared-model

  - name: restricted-model
    storageUri: hf://restricted-org/private-model
    injectHfToken: false
    env:
      - name: HF_TOKEN
        valueFrom:
          secretKeyRef:
            name: restricted-org-token
            key: HF_TOKEN

kubectl create secret generic restricted-org-token \
  -n models --from-literal=HF_TOKEN="$RESTRICTED_TOKEN"

Prefill pools

Prefill containers receive the token automatically, so a disaggregated workload needs no extra configuration:

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-disagg
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
    prefill:
      replicas: 2
      resources:
        limits:
          nvidia.com/gpu: "2"

If you supply containers explicitly under prefill.template, that definition is used verbatim and you provide the environment variable yourself.

Multiple namespaces

The Secret must exist in every namespace that runs a workload:

for ns in models team-a team-b; do
  kubectl create secret generic hf-secret -n "$ns" --from-literal=HF_TOKEN="$HF_TOKEN"
done

Avoiding repeated gated downloads

Mirror the model once into storage you control, then deploy from there. See S3 and air-gapped and Local model cache. Check the model license before redistributing weights internally.

Troubleshooting 

kubectl logs -n models <pod> -c storage-initializer --tail=50
kubectl get secret hf-secret -n models
Message Cause Fix
401 Unauthorized Token missing or invalid Recreate the Secret with a valid token
403 Forbidden License not accepted Accept it with the account owning the token
404 Not Found Wrong repository, or private with no access Check the path and permissions
CreateContainerConfigError Secret missing in this namespace Create it in the workload namespace
Token works locally, not in cluster Wrong namespace or key name Key must be HF_TOKEN
